events.title: The First Council of Nicaea opens
events.shortBlurb: The first ecumenical council of the Church gathered at Nicaea under the Emperor Constantine to answer the Arian denial of Christ’s divinity, and gave the Church its Creed…
body: In the year 325 the Emperor Constantine summoned the bishops of the Christian world to Nicaea in Asia Minor for the first ecumenical council; by tradition the sessions opened on the twentieth of May. Some three hundred bishops, many of them survivors of the recent persecutions, took part.

The council met chiefly to answer the teaching of the priest Arius, who denied that the Son was fully God. Against him it professed the Son to be “consubstantial” (homoousios) with the Father, and it drew up the creed that, expanded, is still recited at Mass. It also fixed a common method for calculating the date of Easter and settled other matters of discipline.

sources.text: Catholic Encyclopedia (1913), “The First Council of Nicaea”

events.title: Ignatius of Loyola is wounded at Pamplona
events.shortBlurb: A cannonball shattered the leg of a Spanish soldier and set in motion the conversion that gave the Church the Jesuits…
body: On 20 May 1521, during the French assault on the citadel of Pamplona, a cannonball struck Íñigo López de Loyola and shattered his leg. The wound ended his career as a soldier and left him to a long and painful convalescence at his family's castle at Loyola.

Having no romances to read, he was given lives of Christ and the saints, and the reading kindled in him a desire to imitate them. From that conversion grew the Spiritual Exercises, the pilgrim years, his studies, and at last the founding of the Society of Jesus — so that the Jesuits trace their origin to the injury of this day.
